projects.name: ThermoScope
projects.problem: A satellite can tell you something is burning at a spot in Gujarat. It can't tell you what caused it.
projects.built: It groups raw NASA FIRMS detections into 20,409 events, adds OpenStreetMap, power-plant and land-cover context, and a LightGBM model labels each as industrial, gas flare, crop residue or wildfire. A map dashboard sits on top, with 496 tests behind it. It's near real time: inference reruns every 30 minutes on the latest live FIRMS data.
projects.credit: Built with Suvarcha Wadhwa. Mentor: Chiranjit Dutta.

screenshots.alt: ThermoScope dashboard: a map of Gujarat with heat events grouped into numbered clusters, filters for predicted class, status and land cover, and a list of recent events labelled crop residue or forest and wildfire.
screenshots.caption: Every detected heat event in Gujarat, clustered on the map

screenshots.alt: ThermoScope detail panel for one event labelled crop residue at 95.2 percent: a close-up map of the site, the observed fire data, the distance to the nearest industrial site and power plant, and the model's probability for each class.
screenshots.caption: One event, with the evidence behind its label

projects.name: Retention Decision Engine
projects.problem: A subscription business can see who already left. It can't tell who's about to, or why.
projects.built: Calibrated LightGBM and survival models predict who will lapse at 7 and 30 days, with per-customer reason codes. Served through FastAPI and Valkey with an MLflow registry, a Streamlit dashboard and about 2,900 tests, all in Docker Compose.

screenshots.alt: Retention dashboard overview: about 3,160 of 169,673 scored customers are expected to lapse in the next 7 days, with expected lapses for days 1 to 7, 8 to 30 and 31 to 59, and bar charts of the main reason codes.

Retention action planner: a line chart of net value against contact budget, comparing the optimiser with highest-risk, random and no-action strategies. At a 5,000 budget the plan contacts 4,887 customers.
Retention model health page: model version 1 with every file matching its registered hash, and a table of calibration slopes and intercepts before and after a fix for the 7 and 30 day horizons.

projects.name: Legal RAG Chatbot
projects.problem: A language model can tell you what the law says. It can't show you where it read it.
projects.built: It answers from indexed Indian statutes and judgments with bracketed citations, then checks that every citation matches a passage it retrieved, retrying or flagging it if not. Built in a week.

screenshots.alt: Terminal window titled Legal Assistant RAG Chatbot, AI Legal Assistant for Indian Law. It lists four modes: Research to ask legal questions, Judgment to simulate or reference judgments, Summarize to generate headnotes or summaries, and Exit, with a prompt waiting for a choice.
screenshots.caption: The chatbot's terminal menu, with modes for research, judgments and summaries

points.title: Pass marks first
points.text: I decide what counts as good enough before I see a single result.

points.title: Misses stay visible
points.text: If a target isn't hit, the report says "not met". I don't tune it until it looks fine.

points.title: Context stays out
points.text: Data that gives the answer away never goes into the model's inputs.

points: Built a basic AI email automation and the frontend of the GDG web page.

traits.name: Curious
traits.text: When a number moves, I want to know why before I trust it.

traits.name: Whimsical
traits.text: I draw small characters in the margins of my notes. A few of them live on this site.

traits.name: Relentless
traits.text: I stay on a problem until it's solved, or until I can say clearly why it isn't.

traits.name: Building with people
traits.text: My best work came from teams: a hackathon partner, a mentor, a club full of first-time builders.
